response.question: What is Workbook Lesson 1 and how do I practice it?
response.answer:
What I can tell you from what's here speaks to the kind of training the Workbook belongs to, rather than to Lesson 1 itself. This is a course in mind training [ab98c6dcb99f9a65], and its lessons are meant to prepare you — if read carefully — for the journey it describes [e7f6fcd57807983e]. Much of its early emphasis is on perception, because perception is only temporary [8a4ddb42986da1d4] and an attribute of the space-time belief [a0f50d31cf9d36a2], something to be set straight before anything can truly be known.

But the actual text of Workbook Lesson 1 — its idea and the specific way you're asked to practice it — isn't in what I have here. I can't give you the lesson's wording or its practice instructions without drawing on something these passages don't contain, and I won't invent that. For the exact idea and the method of applying it, you'd want the Workbook lesson itself in front of you.

response.question: Can you describe God?
response.answer:
To describe God from this teaching: God is the Giver of life [cdad6eaa77d2a85e], and God loves you [e8775eb6bb80b58a]. The Father is greater [9b18f46fa9b7eb3e], and as Creator He has perfect faith in His creations, because He created them [919b31be6a7b9305]. Love is everything [4168538feef0d380].

God's creation is whole, and the mark of that wholeness is holiness [45d7542c352f5747]. You yourself are the work of God, and His work is wholly lovable and wholly loving [736705be8d1dfa40]. In fact the Kingdom of Heaven is you -- what else but you did the Creator create [2e867dcfd97baed2]? Only the Oneness of knowledge is without conflict [3420d0187622a6e6].

These give you God through His giving, His love, His creating, and His relationship to you as His creation. They describe God more by what He does and what He is to you than by setting out His nature in itself -- the fuller description of His formlessness or being as such isn't reached here.

case.question: How are love and fear related in the Course?

response.question: How are love and fear related in the Course?
response.answer:
In the Course, love and fear cannot coexist. They stand as "everything" and "nothing": in the conflict between them, fear is really nothing and love is everything, because whenever light enters darkness, the darkness is abolished [4168538feef0d380]. Fear is always a sign of strain, which arises whenever the will to do conflicts with what you do [eebbfce28c6b056f]. Everyone experiences fear [1e1213de5543ef9f], and fear can be traced to illusion — it is illusion that makes a person fearful, because he knows in his heart it is an illusion, and he exerts enormous efforts to establish its reality [33826e1c2085de25].

Love, by contrast, is what inspires miracles — everything that comes from love is a miracle [4c702336bcd1b814]. And where fear arises from a conflict about willing not to love, the corrective step is to recognize it as an expression of fear and to accept the Atonement as the remedy [b385e07ab930fc06].

Taken together, these point toward a single relationship: fear is the sign that love has been withheld or denied, and the movement away from fear is the acceptance of correction rather than a struggle against the fear itself. That connecting thread is my reading of how these teachings fit, drawn from what each states separately.

case.question: How does God think? What is the Mind of God?

response.question: How does God think? What is the Mind of God?
response.answer:
What's gathered here speaks to God's nature and mind, though it comes at your question more by its edges than its center.

God is the Giver of life [cdad6eaa77d2a85e], and He loves you [e8775eb6bb80b58a]. He knows in His own Being, and His Being experiences His Son's experience; His Love is constantly going out [3b1614103542c399]. The minds He created are meant to communicate fully with Him [3b1614103542c399]. What He created is whole, and the mark of that wholeness is holiness [45d7542c352f5747].

As for the kind of knowing that belongs to God: knowledge is timeless, because certainty is not questionable — you know when you have ceased to ask questions [1c6ca9f8d125db0d]. This is distinct from perception, which changes and depends on time [1c6ca9f8d125db0d]. Truth is always abundant [abd1b87ef5302ce0].

There is also the Mind that belongs to Christ, who is the Son of God [dc56ee622c016f7a]. The Son of God is part of the Holy Trinity, yet the Trinity is one — there is no confusion within its levels, because they are of One Mind and One Will, a Single Purpose that creates perfect integration and establishes the peace of God [d813e5f31f71e596]. The Christ Mind wills from the Soul, not from the ego, and that Mind is yours [0a6e67bfc685801f].

Applied to your question, this points toward a Mind that is one, whole, timeless in its knowing, and continually extending love — but naming that as a direct description of "how God thinks" is my own reading drawn across these teachings, not a single statement any of them makes. The fuller nature of the Mind of God isn't laid out directly in what I have here.

response.question: What is the Atonement?
response.answer:
At its heart, atoning means undoing. The undoing of fear is an essential part of the Atonement value of miracles [a49682f9ca9aa6ee]. The Atonement is the Purpose [1910b050bd79821d], and it is the remedy — something to be accepted [b385e07ab930fc06].

It stands in answer to the separation, which is a better term than the "fall" [61a0797807ca6074], and to the sense of lack that followed it [196c17c8dcb41038]. Where the Atonement works, correction is involved: forgiveness is an empty gesture unless it entails correction [bb8dd5cfa83202da], and the correction of fear is a matter of your own will [07f1f3225efe96ba].

Miracles play their part here — they atone for lack and establish perfect protection, and the forgiven, filled with the Soul, forgive in return [85e9a97cd188972c]. Salvation belongs to this same movement: it is nothing more than right-mindedness, which must be accomplished before One-Mindedness can be restored [82839d0dd037a9c0], and it depends on disinhibiting the Call of God that the ego has repressed [acab9397fd6560f0].

Taken together, these point toward the Atonement as the undoing of fear and lack brought about through correction and forgiveness — but that connecting thread is my own reading of how these pieces fit, not a single statement laid out this way. What's here shows the Atonement by its purpose, its effect, and what it answers; it doesn't give a single formal definition of the term itself.

response.question: What is the ego?
response.answer:
The ego is a man-made attempt to perceive yourself as you wished to be, rather than as you are [9f178f8b19409ac1]. It is nothing more than a part of your belief about yourself [565777c2ba4e3219], and it is not the self [b5003cd44ecacc7d]. Man made the self he calls the ego [99889442ed8d213c].

It is bound up with the separation. The ego depends on the specific [4ed350b2b65dad8f], and the part of the mind that believes in it is the part that believes your existence means you are separate [4ed350b2b65dad8f]. To make something out of a sense of lack is to tacitly imply that you believe in separation [196c17c8dcb41038] -- and separation is a better term than the "fall" [61a0797807ca6074].

Belief itself is an ego function; as long as your origin is open to belief at all, you are regarding it from an ego viewpoint [b5003cd44ecacc7d]. The deepest reach of ego thinking is the belief that there is another way, because that belief carries a hint of recognition that the ego is not the self [b5003cd44ecacc7d]. The illusion a person makes about himself makes him fearful, because in his heart he knows it is an illusion [33826e1c2085de25].

Taken together, these describe the ego as a made, specific, belief-bound image of a separated self that is not what you truly are. They speak less to the ego's relation to attack, guilt, or Atonement; those threads aren't reached here.
